build_command: taskset -c 0-11 lake build CausalScaffold.GluingCausality (3231 jobs, no Causal.* or mathlib rebuild)
reading: DEC-167, hereditary form of the gluing field (OQ-95 OPEN). Precausality.glues_iff_coverGluing proves the hereditary form is exactly the gluing axiom asked at every open U and every open cover of U, i.e. the sheaf clause read per open set. Where the M-only form differs, it is said per label.

labels.label: prop:GX_espace_temps_topo
findings: Under DEC-167 (either form of the field) the uniqueness of ETT.tex:592-594 holds as printed: exactly one glued causality makes every chart of the maximal atlas an isomorphism (existsUnique_gluedCausality_GX, from the strict existsUnique_causality_GX_absolutelyMinimalOn_all). The counterexample GX_maximal_not_unique uses topEnlarge, which is not absolutely minimal, so it is no causality under gluing.
labels.note: Not marked only because the statement is about GluedCausality, which is not yet the library's Causality: once the strict refactor makes Causality glued, this theorem is the closed anchor with no added hypothesis.

labels.label: ex:open_subset
findings: ETT.tex:262 (second sentence) holds AS PRINTED under gluing in the hereditary form: existsUnique_gluedCausality_localIsomorphism (existence by the pull-back, which glues hereditarily along a local homeomorphism when C is hereditarily glued; uniqueness by LocalIsomorphism.unique). In the M-only form only the uniqueness is proved (it needs absolute minimality on N only); existence from an M-only C is NOT proved here, since the pull-back lemma (pullback_absolutelyMinimalOn_all_of_isLocalHomeomorph) needs C absolutely minimal on every open set (cf. transparentLine_pullback_val_not_absolutelyMinimal: the pull-back of an M-only C need not be M-only glued; whether some other M-only glued causality exists is open).

ETT.tex:260 (first sentence): existence holds (GluedCausality.onOpen, onOpen_strongMorphism) but the uniqueness is FALSE even under gluing, contrary to DEC-167's 'holds as printed': not_openSubset_unique refutes '∀ glued C on M, ∀ open W, ∃! glued L on W with the inclusion a strong morphism' on the timelike line with W = ℝ: the restriction and the diagonal causality (diagonalG, which glues) are distinct and both make the inclusion a strong morphism. The cause is that a strong morphism (DEC-10/12) only asks the relations of W to imply those of M; gluing plays no role (OQ-107).

True forms proved under gluing: the restriction is the greatest such causality (le_onOpen_of_strongMorphism), the unique one whose inclusion reflects the relations (eq_onOpen_of_reflects), and the unique glued one for which the inclusion is a local isomorphism (existsUnique_onOpen_localIsomorphism, the first sentence read as the special case of the second).

Under the M-only form of the field, onOpen is not available: the restriction of the transparent-point line to ℝ ∖ {0} is not absolutely minimal (transparentLine_onOpen_not_absolutelyMinimal), so 'an open subset of a topological spacetime carries a topological spacetime structure' with the restricted relations fails in that reading; it holds in the hereditary one.
questions: OQ-107 (open): which uniqueness the first sentence means. Reading taken: none chosen; the printed form is refuted and the three readings (greatest; reflecting; local isomorphism) are all proved.
OQ-95 (open): hereditary vs M-only field; the first sentence's existence of the restricted structure needs the hereditary one.
M-only form: does a local homeomorphism onto an M-only glued spacetime always admit an M-only glued causality making it a local isomorphism? Not settled (the pull-back can fail).

labels.label: rem:deux_pushup
findings: ETT.tex:316 ('neither implies the other', also ETT.tex:303-304 'logically independent') is FALSE under gluing, in either form of the field: on every T1 space a glued causally plain causality has the push-up property (GluedCausality.pushUp_of_causallyPlain), so the printed independence is refuted already over ℝ (not_deux_pushup_neither). Strongest true form (deux_pushup_glued): causal plainness implies push-up, strictly — the lightlike line glues, is causal, has push-up and is not plain (the remark's first half stands). The library's no-gluing witness deuxPushup does not glue (deuxPushup_not_glues). The sentence 'causal plainness ... is silent at a point whose causal future or past has empty interior' (ETT.tex:319-320) is therefore no argument for the converse half; suggested wording: 'causal plainness implies the push-up property, not conversely'.

labels.label: cexemple:point_transparent
findings: Re-read under gluing (hereditary form): every computation of the counterexample holds for the precausality (causally plain, absolutely minimal on ℝ, not on ℝ ∖ {0}: strict point_transparent), but 'This is a topological spacetime' (ETT.tex:478) is FALSE: the transparent-point line does not glue (transparentLine_not_glues; not_exists_gluedCausality_transparentLine). The sentence it illustrates, 'Absolute minimality is not inherited by open subsets' (ETT.tex:470), is false for glued causalities (every open subset of one, with the restricted causality, is glued, hence absolutely minimal: point_transparent_glued) and true for precausalities. So under DEC-167 the counterexample belongs to the precausality layer, where DEC-172 already puts rem:minimalite_non_hereditaire; what it shows about causalities is that absolute minimality on M does not imply the gluing clause (M-only ≠ hereditary).

Under the M-only form the line IS a causality, and its restriction to ℝ ∖ {0} is none (transparentLine_onOpen_not_absolutelyMinimal): the example then stands as printed but breaks ex:open_subset's restriction.
questions: OQ-95 decides which re-reading is the one of record: hereditary (the example moves to precausalities, ETT.tex:478 false) or M-only (the example stands; open subsets of spacetimes are not spacetimes with the restricted relations). Reading taken: hereditary, both proved.

refactor_plan.summary: Turn Causal.Causality into the glued notion by adding the field `glues : toPrecausality.Glues` (hereditary form, pending OQ-95) to the structure in Causal/Causality.lean:77, so every full name Causal.Causality.* keeps resolving; the current structure survives under a new name as the no-gluing underlying notion.
steps: 1 (design, T-abs-gluing-design): rule OQ-95 (hereditary recommended: glues_iff_coverGluing shows it is the sheaf gluing axiom at every open set; onOpen, pullback and chartTransport need it) and OQ-96 (fate of the non-gluing objects).

2 (retype, T-abs-gluing-retype): introduce the no-gluing notion as a new structure, e.g. Causal.Precausality.WithChrono or Causal.Causality₀ (Precausality + le_of_lt + isOpen_lt_right/left: exactly today's Causality), in Causal/Causality.lean; move to it, beside the old names, every object that does not glue: gateLine (GateLineLocal), jumpLine (PushUpNotOpen), globalLine (ChronalNeighbourBridge, ChronalTarentin), deuxPushup (DeuxPushup), timelikeLineTop (Morphism), Causality.topEnlarge (GXStructure), transparentLine (TransparentLine), galileoOn for n ≥ 1 (Galileo), pointedLine(MR), doubledLine, puncturedPlane, totalLine, orderLine, allRelated, bowtie, fan, linearCausality ℕ, DensWitness.{densCausality,bigCausality,wideCausality,far2Causality}, arcCausality of a discontinuous arc, and the constructor Causality.ofRelation (LinesReachable:184; it glues only on the diagonal). Their separation theorems become statements about the no-gluing notion (finding history kept). Split conjoined theorems: Causal.deux_pushup (keep the lightlike half), GX_maximal_not_unique, openSubset_not_unique (its diagonal half survives: the diagonal glues), localIsomorphism_not_unique, gateLine_cauchyInclusion_not_causallyConvex.

3 (field, T-abs-gluing-field, atomic): add the field; fill it at the 115 def/abbrev sites of type Causality in the strict library (grep 2026-11-27) and the scaffold, from Causal.GluingGeneric.* (dual, transport, relativeTo, extend, generated with hereditary pieces, pullback along open maps, pushout and family gluings, chartTransport, GX) and Causal.GluingModels.* (concrete models). LocalCausality W (Causal/Local.lean:47) gains the matching field `∀ W' ≤ W, L.extend.AbsolutelyMinimalOn W'` so that Causality.restrict and LocalCausality.toSubtype carry it (Causality.restrict_toSubtype_absolutelyMinimalOn_all). Precausality.generated needs hereditary pieces (generated_single_transparentLine). This file's GluedCausality becomes an abbreviation of Causality (or is deleted), and its theorems move verbatim with `.toCausality` dropped.

4 (theorems): add one-line theorems Causality.absolutelyMinimal and Causality.absolutelyMinimalOn (from the field); keep every theorem with an AbsolutelyMinimal hypothesis unchanged (182 binders `(h… : ….AbsolutelyMinimal)` in 106 strict files mention absolute minimality) and add hypothesis-free corollaries for the ETT rows: existsUnique_causality_GX_maximal without the minimality clause (prop:GX_espace_temps_topo closed and markable), LocalIsomorphism.unique without m₁ m₂ (ex:open_subset second sentence closed), Causality.pushUp_of_causallyPlain on T1 spaces (rem:deux_pushup, the refutation of the converse half), lem:precausalite_restriction_minimale and rem:minimalite_non_hereditaire become statements about precausalities (DEC-172).

kb_proposals: The hereditary form of gluing ∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W is exactly the per-open-set gluing axiom Precausality.CoverGluing (glues_iff_coverGluing, CausalScaffold.GluingCausality): cite it as the sheaf reading of defi:causalite.

Under gluing, ex:open_subset's first-sentence uniqueness is still false (diagonalG glues); prop:GX_espace_temps_topo holds as printed in either form; its second sentence holds as printed in the hereditary form (uniqueness also M-only); rem:deux_pushup's independence is false (plain ⇒ push-up on T1); the transparent-point line is no glued causality. All in CausalScaffold.GluingCausality, written over GluedCausality so they move verbatim at the field switch.
